channel.title: Onchain Report
channel.description: Crypto news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation, security incidents and network upgrades across the blockchain industry.

item.title: Consensys and ClearToken target 24/7 institutional settlement
item.description: Consensys and ClearToken will work on 24/7 settlement for tokenised securities and cash, aiming to connect blockchain speed with the legal controls institutions need.

item.title: Ledger reviews reseller rules after crypto wallet theft
item.description: Ledger is reviewing reseller and anti-tamper controls after an implant was found in a wallet tied to a crypto theft estimated at about $90 million.

item.title: Judge keeps Gemini’s $5 million CFTC settlement in place
item.description: A Manhattan judge has kept Gemini’s $5 million CFTC settlement in place, ruling that a later shift in enforcement policy does not justify reopening the case.

item.title: How to fund a wallet on a new network
item.description: To fund a wallet on a new network, match the chain and token, choose a transfer route, and leave enough of the network’s native coin to pay fees.

item.title: Swap Into a Liquid Asset Before You Bridge
item.description: Swapping into an asset with deep liquidity and bridge support can make a cross-chain move easier, but the best choice depends on the route and destination.

item.title: Recover Your Wallet Before Swapping Stablecoins
item.description: Recover wallet access before swapping: stablecoins usually stay on their network, while a swap can add fees, slippage and extra steps to the recovery process.

item.title: Coinbase and Marqeta team up on stablecoin-backed cards
item.description: Coinbase will hold stablecoins and convert them for Marqeta card programs, while Base handles settlement, giving businesses a new way for customers to spend.

item.title: How to fund recurring Bitcoin payments with Monero
item.description: To fund recurring Bitcoin bills from Monero, swap XMR into BTC before each due date, then keep enough in your payment wallet for the invoice and network fee.

item.title: Why a gas quote can change during a transfer
item.description: A gas quote is an estimate or cap, while the network price can move before a transaction is included. Know what your wallet fixes before you confirm.

item.title: How to Fund a Liquidity Pool Across Chains
item.description: Funding a pool across chains means getting the right tokens onto the pool’s network, then depositing them; bridges add cost, delay and separate risks.

item.title: Set a Minimum Before You Make a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: Cross-chain swaps can return less than the quote when prices or pool depth shift. Set a minimum output you can accept, then check fees and route risk.

item.title: Why redeeming a wrapped asset can take one more transaction
item.description: Redeeming a wrapped token can take a burn, a release, and sometimes a separate claim; knowing which step is pending helps prevent duplicate actions on the source chain.

item.title: Check the Address Before You Bridge Crypto
item.description: EVM chains can share an address format, while other networks use different ones. Check the destination chain and address before you approve a bridge transfer.

item.title: How Bridging Funds Can Make Crypto Usable as Collateral
item.description: Bridging can put crypto on the chain where a lending market accepts it, but the token, bridge design and debt rules decide whether it works and at what cost.

item.title: How to fund a Mantle NFT mint
item.description: To mint an NFT on Mantle, move the right token to the network, keep MNT for fees and check that the funds arrived before you connect to the mint.

item.title: Three Ways to Recover a Bridge When Gas Runs Low
item.description: When a bridge stalls because gas runs low, first find which step is stuck, then top up, speed up a pending transaction, or use the bridge’s recovery path.

item.title: Compare the Route, Not Just the Cross-Chain Quote
item.description: A cross-chain quote is more than its output number: compare fees, route steps, timing, and what arrives on the destination chain before you approve.

item.title: How businesses should track cross-chain crypto transfers
item.description: A cross-chain transfer can split records across ledgers. Businesses need one joined trail showing ownership, value, fees and each step of the transfer.

item.title: Starknet asks holders to study an independent post-quantum chain
item.description: Starknet is asking STRK holders whether to study an independent, post-quantum Layer 1, a move that could give it more control over security work tied to Ethereum.

item.title: When One Cross-Chain Swap Route Beats Two
item.description: A cross-chain swap can bundle a bridge and a trade into one route, but splitting the steps may give better control, clearer costs and fewer surprises.
